chunks: Fasting is not permissible during the days of Tashriq, for they are days of eating, drinking, and conjugal relations.
The Sunnah is to break the fast on the day of sacrifice (Eid al-Adha) after returning from the prayer, and on Eid al-Fitr before going out to the prayer.

The Takbir during the days of Tashriq in Mina is [recommended] after fifteen prayers, from Thuhr on the day of sacrifice until the dawn prayer on the fourth day; and in other cities, after ten prayers, from Thuhr on the day of sacrifice until the dawn prayer on the third day.

key_terms.أيام التشريق: The three days after Eid al-Adha (11th-13th Dhul-Hijja), named for the drying of sacrificial meat in the sun
key_terms.التكبير: The saying of 'Allahu Akbar' (God is greatest), specifically the ritual Takbir after prayers during Hajj season
key_terms.الغداة: The dawn/morning prayer (Fajr), using the classical term
key_terms.دبر الصلاة: After the obligatory prayer (used to specify when Takbir is recommended)

ai.seo_question: Is fasting allowed during the days of Tashriq in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This narration presents a legal ruling (fatwa) on three interconnected Hajj-related practices: the prohibition of fasting during the days of Tashriq (11th-13th Dhul-Hijja), the proper Sunnah timing for breaking fast on the two Eid days, and the prescribed duration for reciting the Takbir (Allahu Akbar) after obligatory prayers. Pilgrims in Mina recite Takbir for a longer period (fifteen prayers) than those in other cities (ten prayers), reflecting the special sacred status of the Hajj site. These rulings were transmitted from early Shia jurisprudence and represent the scholarly tradition of Shaykh al-Saduq in codifying fiqh.

en.bilal-muhammad: Fasting is not permissible during the days of tashriq, for they are days of eating, drinking, and bathing.
The sunna is to break your fast on the [Eid] day of sacrifice after coming back from prayer; and before going out to pray on [Eid] al-Fitr.

Takbir [is recommended] in the days of tashriq after fifteen prayers, from Thuhr on the day of sacrifice to [Fajr] on the fourth day; and after ten prayers in other cities, from Thuhr on the day of sacrifice to [Fajr] on the third day.
